stories.headline: UGC-NET results announced for 84 subjects; over 4,000 qualify for JRF
stories.deck: The testing agency had also issued a special notice concerning the Sociology, Commerce and English papers after an expert committee found factual, typographical, translation and language-related errors in the question papers.
stories.bodyText:
The results of the UGC National Eligibility Test (NET) for 84 subjects have been announced, with more than 4,000 candidates qualifying for the Junior Research Fellowship, the National Testing Agency has said.
“Out of 6.07 lakh candidates who appeared for the exam in 84 subjects, over 97,000 have qualified for PhD admissions and over 4,000 for JRF,” a senior NTA official said late on Friday (August 28, 2026).
The examinations were conducted in June, with the NTA releasing the UGC-NET answer key on August 16, nearly two months after the examination. The testing agency had also issued a special notice concerning the Sociology, Commerce and English papers after an expert committee found factual, typographical, translation and language-related errors in the question papers.
Later, on the same day (August 16), it announced that the three examinations would be conducted afresh in September, citing the errors.
The re-examinations are scheduled for September 9 and 10, for which candidates will not be required to pay an additional fee.
The NET is conducted by the NTA to determine the eligibility of Indian nationals for the role of assistant professor and for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) in Indian universities and colleges.

stories.headline: PM Modi begins four-day Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit for SCO summit; what's on agenda
stories.deck: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. He will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent. Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister 
Narendra Modi
 on Saturday embarked on a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic, during which he will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek.
PM Modi will be on a State Visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30 at the invitation of Mirziyoyev before travelling to Bishkek for the SCO summit on August 31 and September 1.
In his departure statement, the Prime Minister said the visit would focus on strengthening India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia and deepening its ties with the region.
Talks with Mirziyoyev in Tashkent
During his visit to Tashkent, PM Modi will hold delegation-level talks with President Mirziyoyev to further strengthen the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership.
The two leaders will review cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, education and people-to-people ties, and set the agenda for future engagement.
“I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan,” PM Modi said.
This will be PM Modi's fourth visit to Uzbekistan.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.
PM Modi described the two visits as a tribute to the “close cultural and people-to-people ties” between India and Uzbekistan.
PM Modi to visit Bishkek for SCO summit
From Tashkent, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to attend the 26th SCO Summit, which marks 25 years of the organisation.
India has been a full and active member of the SCO since 2017.
“I look forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in our neighbourhood and beyond,” PM Modi said.
The Prime Minister is expected to meet President Zhaparov and other SCO leaders and will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.
Putin, Xi among leaders expected at summit
Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are among the leaders expected to attend the two-day SCO summit in Bishkek.
The summit will bring together leaders of the 10-member grouping, which includes Russia, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, four Central Asian countries and Belarus.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif are also expected to participate in the plenary session.
The SCO, which was founded with a focus on regional and economic cooperation, now has 15 dialogue partners and two observer countries, Afghanistan and Mongolia.
PM Modi said he was confident that his visit would “strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen our civilisational connect with the region, and advance our shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity.”

stories.headline: TCS techie on way home dies after reversing JCB rams his bike in Gurgaon
stories.deck: A 27-year-old systems engineer died after a reversing earthmover struck his motorcycle. The incident occurred late Thursday night near Moulsari Avenue Rapid Metro station. Tushar Kumar was returning home from his work at Tata Consultancy Services. His father alleged the road work lacked proper directions and indicators. Police have seized the earthmover and are examining the allegations.
stories.bodyText:
GURGAON: A 27-year-old systems engineer with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Tushar Kumar, was killed late Thursday night after a reversing earthmover engaged in road work rammed into his motorcycle near Moulsari Avenue Rapid Metro station.
The machine’s driver fled the spot.
Tushar was returning home from work around 11.30pm when his Royal Enfield was hit by the JCB earthmover’s rear bucket.
The impact threw him and the bike onto the road. He was rushed to Narayana Hospital in DLF Phase 3, where doctors declared him dead. He was wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.
Sources said GMDA was carrying out routine maintenance work at the site.
Tushar had been working in the city for four years and was staying with his uncle in Ramprastha City, Sector 37D, while his parents lived in Mathura. He was their only child.
Police said a passerby informed them about the incident around 11.45pm.
“He usually left work around the same time every day. He had bought the bike about a year ago and would use it to travel to and from work. We never imagined that one day he would leave for work and not return,” said his father, Harish Kumar.
Harish said police informed him of the accident, and he reached the hospital around 3.30am, where he identified his son’s body at the mortuary.
“I reached the hospital and saw my son there. He was our only child. We had sent him to Gurgaon to work and build his future,” he said.
In his complaint, Harish alleged that the work was being carried out at night in the middle of the road without proper directions or indicators. Police said they are examining this allegation.
A police officer said that on receiving information from the hospital, a team reached the spot and found the JCB, bearing registration number HR-36-AN-7050, abandoned. The JCB has been seized.

briefs.headline: Will call for bandh in Bengaluru: Private transport operators
briefs.bodyText:
The Federation of Private Transport Organisations has staged a protest against taxi aggregators and other issues concerning private transport operators in the city.
It has submitted a complaint to the Transport Commissioner on Friday seeking restrictions on taxi apps on the Play Store and other market places, implementation of a “One City, One Fare” system, and criminal action against unlicensed companies.
Federation president Nataraj Sharma said a 15-day deadline has been given to the government to address their demands.
If no action is taken, the federation will call for a Bengaluru bandh, he said, adding that the protest would begin with private transport operators displaying black flags on their vehicles.

briefs.headline: Sandhya Devanathan exits Meta after a decade; to join OpenAI as VP South East Asia, Australia
briefs.deck: Sandhya Devanathan, is leaving the social media giant and is all set to join OpenAI as Vice President for South East Asia and Australia
briefs.bodyText:
Meta's Vice President and Head for India and South East Asia, Sandhya Devanathan, is leaving the social media giant after more than a decade and is all set to join OpenAI as Vice President for South East Asia and Australia.
In this newly-created role, Devanathan will be OpenAI’s most senior leader in South East Asia and Australia, with responsibility for its performance across consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations.
The Meta veteran penned an emotional post on LinkedIn, announcing her departure from the social media giant and said she is looking forward to her "next exciting chapter". She, however, did not divulge her next move.
OpenAI confirmed that Devanathan will join as Vice President for Southeast Asia and Australia. She will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI's Managing Director for Asia Pacific, the ChatGPT-maker confirmed.
Devanathan's joining date at OpenAI could not be immediately ascertained.
Notably, the appointment comes as OpenAI expands its presence across Asia Pacific amid growing adoption of its AI tools among consumers, enterprises and developers.
Over the past two years, OpenAI has opened local offices in Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney and Delhi, and expanded its regional leadership team with the recent appointment of Kiran Mani as Managing Director for APAC.
In June this year, the Sam Altman-led company announced the appointment of Prabhjeet Singh as Managing Director for India, among its top-priority markets and one where the company has been stepping up investments and expanding its footprint.
In fact, OpenAI has been moving its India strategy to top gear through partnerships with enterprises and developers, while strengthening engagement with policymakers. The company opened its first office in New Delhi in November 2025.
Altman himself has repeatedly described India as one of OpenAI's key markets and has praised the country's rapid AI uptake and commitment to investing across the tech stack.
Devanathan brings more than 25 years of experience across the technology and financial services sectors. She joined Meta in 2016 and held several leadership roles across the region, including leading its Asia Pacific gaming business and helping expand the company's presence in Singapore and Vietnam.
In the LinkedIn post, Devanathan described the decision to leave after more than a decade as "bittersweet" and said she would take a short break before beginning her "next exciting chapter".
Looking back at her tenure, she highlighted Meta's work with businesses, startups and creators across the region, including government citizen services on WhatsApp in India and helping small businesses establish storefronts on its apps in Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand.
"I joined Meta when we had just about 300 employees in Singapore," she recounted and reflected on how the landscape looked "so different" in 2016, with everyone talking about digital transformation.
"And we were right in the midst of it - helping startups, companies, creators and the ecosystem grow across the region while delivering great experiences for hundreds of millions of our users," she wrote.
Devanathan said she was "incredibly proud" of what her teams had built and thanked colleagues, businesses, ecosystem partners, non-profits and creators she had worked with during her time at Meta.
"Over the years, I’ve had the privilege of working across sectors like ecommerce and gaming in APAC, and leading talented teams across India and Southeast Asia. Throughout this journey, I’ve been fueled by the belief that our work brings meaningful connections to people and businesses worldwide," she further said.
Describing the day as "emotional", Devanathan said the teams she worked with were nothing short of exceptional and made this an incredible ride.
"I shared with my teams today that I am extraordinarily proud of how they've shown up every day, doing the best work they can in an industry that is rapidly evolving. I’m proud of the work we’ve done together - be the millions of people using government citizen services on WA (WhatsApp) in India or the millions of small businesses in Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand who opened their storefronts on our apps or helping startups become unicorns in Singapore, Malaysia and Philippines...the stories are many and I am incredibly proud of everything we’ve built together," she said.

briefs.headline: Congress alleges Penguin India succumbed to ‘pressure’ to demand changes in Sonia memoir
briefs.deck: Congress leader Ashok Gehlot claims Penguin India sought to remove sections critical of the PM, the RSS, and China’s “occupation“ of Indian land; says Penguin Worldwide was willing to publish the book unchanged for global audience
briefs.bodyText:
Congress leaders on Friday (August 28, 2026) accused Penguin Random House India of giving in to pressure over the publication of former Congress president Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, with senior party leader Ashok Gehlot alleging that the publisher sought to remove portions critical of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and the alleged “occupation” of Indian territory by China.
The Congress reactions came after Penguin Random House India issued a statement, saying that “fact-checking and editorial recommendations” were part of its normal publishing process.
“Penguin Worldwide is ready to publish Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji’s upcoming book worldwide in its original form, but Penguin Random House India wants changes made to launch it in India. After all, what is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?” Mr. Gehlot said in a post on X.
‘Murder of democracy’
He said Ms. Gandhi’s “integrity and dignity” in public life were exemplary and alleged that suppressing her book under pressure amounted to a “murder of freedom of expression”.
“The real issue is that pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Modi, the RSS, and the occupation of Indian territory by China during Modi’s rule. This is the murder of democracy,” he alleged.
Former Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Kamal Nath termed the publisher’s refusal to bring out the memoir in India a matter of “grave concern” and questioned whether the decision had been taken independently.
“Will the publisher decide what a senior figure like Mrs. Gandhi will write and what she will not? The question also arises whether the publisher is saying this on its own or if there is pressure from someone on it?” Mr. Nath said.
‘Editorial independence compromised’
Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi described Penguin India’s statement on the controversy as “weak”.
“Such a weak statement. Penguin India is more than happy to publish Exam Warriors [written by Mr. Modi] and several books on the RSS. No doubt there are those in the BJP government who have now become afraid of a book being read by the people of India,” Mr. Gogoi said on X.
Congress Seva Dal chief B.V. Srinivas also attacked the publishing house, accusing it of compromising its editorial independence.
“Dear Modi’s Penguin, godi mein baithkar ‘editorial independence’ bolna thoda funny lagta hai. Reed ki haddi hoti toh publisher kehlate [Dear Modi’s Penguin, it sounds funny when you talk about ‘editorial independence’ while sitting on the lap. If you had a spine, you would have been called a publisher],” Mr. Srinivas said in a post on X.

briefs.headline: Fresh glacial lakes form at source of Nepal’s ice-rock avalanche
briefs.deck: NDMA head confirms the formation of two new lakes and moraines, but says no information is available on water volume; monitoring limitations mean that early warning systems may not be able to prevent another such disaster
briefs.bodyText:
Two more glacial lakes have formed in Nepal, near the apparent source of the ice-rock avalanche that triggered flooding in Nepal’s Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river system on Wednesday (August 26, 2026).
Also read: Nepal flash flood updates on August 28, 2026
While the formation of the lakes is known, information on the potential water outflow is unavailable, said Krishna Vatsa, Member and Head of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). “One is 19.80 hectares, and the other is 7.28 hectares. We don’t have any estimates of the volume, but there are moraines [piles of debris deposited by a moving glacier],” he told The Hindu. “These are lakes that have formed in Nepal, and we don’t have direct knowledge of what’s happening there. We need to keep monitoring. These are natural formations, and so we can’t entirely predict how they evolve,” he added.
At least one of these lakes appears similar to the one independently confirmed by Suhora Technologies, a Noida-based space-data analytics firm, which also said it had identified a “newly formed water body” at the source of the ice-rock avalanche.
Monitoring new glacial lake
“Analysis of high-resolution optical satellite imagery acquired on August 27 shows a lake spanning approximately 20.25 hectares in the high-altitude Lhende Khola region, near the Nepal-Tibet border. The company placed the feature at 28°17′39.0″N, 85°30′38.9″E. The imagery, supplied by Satellogic at a resolution of about 70 cm, was acquired at 04:22 UTC (9:52 a.m. IST) on August 27,” the company said in a statement on Friday.
Suhora said the lake’s formation is an important feature to monitor following the August 26 avalanche and subsequent flash flooding downstream. While a newly formed water body in the vicinity of an avalanche or debris-flow source could indicate water accumulation associated with the event, its presence by itself does not mean that another glacial-lake outburst flood is imminent.
The company said it would continue monitoring the lake’s extent and stability using satellite imagery. The assessment remains preliminary, and further observations and ground-based investigation will be needed to establish the lake’s origin, depth, stability, and potential downstream risk, it added.
‘No escape’
So far, the consensus among experts is that a mass of glacier ice, rock, and debris in the Himalayas near Langtang Lirung detached itself at about 5,200 metres and fell roughly 1,200 metres into the Lhende Khola system. Its momentum gathered more rock, sediment, ice, and water and morphed it into a fast-moving debris flow. This is what inundated the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river system.
ALSO WATCH Nepal flash floods: What the disaster means for China-Nepal infrastructure and diplomacy?
NDMA officials said that India had a monitoring network of both ground and satellite measurements that “were being improved”. However, there are still limitations. “We can give early warning 30 to 45 minutes in advance, and that can save lives, but when billions of litres of water gush, there is no escape. Damage can be contained only when there are restrictions on the construction and infrastructure in the vulnerable river basins in the path of such outflow,” an official connected to the Centre’s disaster management body told The Hindu.

briefs.headline: High-powered task force looking into NTA reforms invites stakeholder suggestions
briefs.deck: The Nandan Nilekani-led task force set up by PM Narendra Modi requested stakeholders to submit their suggestions by Sept. 13; submissions can be made in English, Hindi or regional languages by phone, mail, WhatsApp or website
briefs.bodyText:
A high-powered task force constituted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to recommend reforms in public examinations has invited suggestions from stakeholders, including students, parents, teachers and academic institutions as part of a public consultation exercise.
Stakeholders like examination-conducting and test-indenting bodies, subject matter experts and technology professionals, industry and civil society organisations as well as others can also submit their suggestions.
“As part of this exercise, the task force considers it extremely useful to benefit from the experience, knowledge and perspectives of all stakeholders,” said an official statement by the Ministry of Personnel.
The task force under former UIDAI chairman Nandan Nilekani was constituted after the widely criticised leak of National Eligibility Cum Entrance Test (NEET) undergraduate 2026 exam paper, which is a gateway for sought after MBBS admissions in medical colleges. Prior to this, the Centre had constituted a committee under former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan, following the leak of NEET-UG 2024 paper with a view to overhaul the public examination system.
Supreme Court stricture
Earlier this month, the Supreme Court warned the Centre against “committee hopping”, stating that NTA reforms must build permanent institutional memory rather than changing with every new panel. The top court had also asked the government to explain how the task force led by Mr. Nilekani interacts with, modifies or nuances earlier recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan Committee.
The task force has stated that suggestions may relate to conduct and security of public examinations, examination design and assessment methodology, governance, accountability and institutional arrangements, prevention, detection and redressal of examination malpractices. It has also invited suggestions on use of technology, including secure computer-based testing as well as creation and augmentation of examination infrastructure.
Suggestions are also invited on inclusive examination framework for better access across social, economic, regional and linguistic groups.
The task force has also asked suggestions on how to institute transparency, grievance redressal and stakeholder communication as well as measures to promote student well-being throughout the examination process and any other measure that may add value in the examination system.
The task force has requested that the stakeholders should submit their suggestions by September 13. Submissions may be made in English, Hindi or regional languages, the official statement notes.
“The inputs received through this public consultation will assist the high-powered task force in formulating its recommendations to the government,” the statement further says.
“The task force is examining measures for strengthening institutional systems and processes, ensuring examination integrity and security, deploying appropriate technologies, augmenting examination infrastructure, promoting accessibility and inclusion, as well as safeguarding student well-being,” the official statement says. “The objective is to develop a robust, secure, transparent, equitable and future-ready public examination system.”
This includes examining and recommending comprehensive reforms relating to the conduct, security, design and governance of public examinations, including examinations conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA).
Suggestions can be sent in by accessing the website: https://examreforms-taskforce.dopt.gov.in, and by phone 1800-180-4747. Alternatively, they can also send a WhatsApp text “hptf” to +917827042830 or email at ExamReformsTaskforce@dopt.gov.in.

briefs.headline: CPI-CPI(M) tussle over Deputy Opposition Leader post in Keralam is a mutiny against Pinarayi Vijayan
briefs.deck: The issue is not so much about the ‘nominal’ post as it is about the clamour for collective leadership; in other words, it is a mutiny against the Leader of the Opposition, whose absolute authority has been resented by the CPI over the last decade and a half
briefs.bodyText:
The no-holds-barred public wrangling between the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] and the Communist Party of India (CPI), the two major constituents of the Left Democratic Front (LDF), over the post of Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Keralam Assembly is not so much about the ‘nominal’ post as it is about the clamour for collective leadership. In other words, it is a mutiny against Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, whose absolute authority has been resented by the CPI over the last decade and a half.
What is new now is that sections of the CPI(M) at the district, area and local committee levels have come to share some of these concerns pertaining to concentration of power, which they think has enfeebled the party and the front and its broad support base, more so in the wake of the crushing defeat suffered by the LDF in the Assembly elections early this year.
This was evident in the post-mortem undertaken by the CPI(M) in what was described by party general secretary M.A. Baby as an honest attempt to get to the root of the reasons for the LDF’s poll debacle. The CPI, too, embarked on a similar exercise in which its leadership faced uneasy questions.
But not everyone in these parties is upbeat about the possible outcomes of the exercise. The lower rungs of the CPI(M), for instance, are peeved about being excluded from the extended State committee meeting in Kozhikode from September 13, although it includes State-level representatives from the party’s mass and class organisations. They are also at a loss to defend the slew of financial allegations against T. Veena, Mr. Vijayan’s daughter.
But the CPI’s grouse is far older and deep-rooted. In the last 10 years, with an LDF government led by Mr. Vijayan in place, there have been several run-ins between the CPI and the CPI(M) over encounter killings of suspected Maoists, the anti-encroachment drive in Munnar, slapping of UAPA, the SilverLine railway project, and the like.
But Kodiyeri Balakrishnan and Kanam Rajendran, who helmed their respective parties in the State, were able to bury the hatchet soon. Kanam’s successor, Binoy Viswam, the present CPI State secretary, faced criticism from within initially for kowtowing to Mr. Vijayan.
PM SHRI issue
But the CPI’s stiff opposition to the LDF government signing up for PM SHRI without even a perfunctory discussion within the front opened a new war front, forcing the government to backtrack. CPI(M) leaders accuse the CPI of feigning ideological purity, while the CPI sees the CPI(M) — Mr. Vijayan specifically — as authoritarian and not democratic enough.
Sources say that Mr. Vijayan, who has been given multiple exemptions by the CPI(M) for organisational and parliamentary roles, will eventually step down from the post of Opposition Leader, but no timeline has been set.
CPI(M) central committee member K.N. Balagopal is the party’s choice for Deputy Leader of the Opposition, while the CPI is rooting for its parliamentary party leader, K. Rajan. The alliance partners are unanimous about the lack of a united Opposition agenda on the floor of the Assembly, which was stark during the first session of the present 16th Assembly.
Against Mr. Vijayan’s assertion of having a CPI(M) Deputy Leader of the Opposition, LDF convener T.P. Ramakrishnan was more diplomatic, choosing the path of dialogue. The CPI, meanwhile, remains unrelenting in its demand for a change. Veteran leader C. Divakaran says nobody has a monopoly over the Left. Clearly, the guns are trained on Mr. Vijayan.
Published - August 29, 2026 07:00 am IST

briefs.headline: U.S. diplomats and family members slowly begin to return to West Asian embassies
briefs.deck: We remain committed to supporting our workforce and their families throughout this process and will provide updates through appropriate channels as decisions are made, said the U.S. State Department
briefs.bodyText:
American diplomats and at least some of their family members are beginning to return to U.S.embassies in West Asia after many were ordered to leave their posts during the early days of the war with Iran.
Although most embassies are not returning to full strength immediately, starting this week the State Department has begun to lift certain staffing and other restrictions on personnel.
The changes are not necessarily reflective of a shift in the Trump administration's policy toward Iran — now focused on economic rather than kinetic military warfare. Instead, the changes are mainly due to the legalities of human resources policy, which limits the time diplomats may be away from post while still being paid and collecting benefits for themselves and their families.
On Friday (August 28), the day the Iran war hit its six-month mark, embassies in Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain announced they would allow diplomats' family members to return, although in Bahrain and Kuwait it applies only to those older than 18.
Earlier in the week, all family members of U.S. government employees in Israel, as well as those who are over 21 and who work in Lebanon, were given the go-ahead to return.
These embassies were all placed on “ordered departure” or “authorized departure” status in March as Iran began retaliating for U.S. and Israeli attacks by targeting U.S. interests, including embassies and military facilities, and creating chaotic situations in countries around the region.
Ordered departure means that all nonessential personnel and families must leave the country. Authorized departure means that staff deemed nonessential and their families may leave.
However, regulations time-limit those statuses, which were beginning to expire six months after being initiated, meaning affected diplomats and their families would be losing their housing and other benefits, creating significant hardships among the workforce.
To deal with this, the State Department created a new status — that of “restricted operations” — which is designed to allow the embassies to resume normal functions. On a case-by-case basis, each affected embassy will make its own determination on appropriate staffing, the presence of families and pay and benefits.
Diplomats and their families were ordered to leave embassies in another five countries in the region early in the war, and changes in status at some of them also were anticipated soon.
“We remain committed to supporting our workforce and their families throughout this process and will provide updates through appropriate channels as decisions are made,” the department said.

stories.headline: Bengaluru court sentences eight persons to life imprisonment in 2017 murder case
stories.bodyText:
A Bengaluru court has sentenced eight men to rigorous life imprisonment for the murder of Harish, who was killed following a quarrel over smoking near his house during the Vijayadashami celebrations in 2017.
In a press note, Public Prosecutor Mahalingappa Uttura stated that the 58th Additional City Civil and Sessions Court, presided over by judge Sujata M. Sambrani, convicted all accused on Thursday. They were sentenced to rigorous life imprisonment under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The convicted are Gerald Arogyaraj, James Kumar, Venkatesh, Vijay, Kiran, Vikram, and two minors.
According to the statement, the incident occurred in the Ashok Nagar Police Station limits on October 1, 2017. Around 12.30 a.m., Harish, who stepped out to watch the Vijayadashami procession, saw three men smoking and talking loudly near his house. When he objected to them smoking there and creating a nuisance, an argument broke out. Harish allegedly assaulted the trio and warned them against returning.
The three later informed other accused that Harish had assaulted them. Subsequently, a few days later, the accused allegedly decided to kill Harish and waylaid him near his house. One accused allegedly attacked him with a machete while another stabbed him in the back. The others assisted them. Two accused allegedly crushed his head with a stone, resulting in his death.
The court also awarded additional sentences under IPC Sections 144, 148, 149, and 341. A total of ₹3.9 lakh from the fines is to be paid to Harish’s family.

stories.headline: Row over smoking: Eight men get life imprisonment for killing youth in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A local court held eight men guilty of hacking a 32-year-old man to death after he objected to some of them smoking in public, and sentenced them to life imprisonment.
The convicts are Venkatesh M, B Vijay alias Kari Vijay, R Vinod Kumar, Gerald Arokiya Raj, R Kiran alias Dikky, I Vikram, James Kumar and S Vijay alias Kotanguchhi, all residents of Viveknagar, central Bengaluru.
Public prosecutor Mahalingappa Uttura said the speciality of the case was five witnesses identifying the eight accused during identification parade without making any mistake. “The parade was done thrice at Central Prison in the presence of a tahsildar. Each time, the accused were made to stand in a different line and in different orders. However, the five witnesses — the victim’s mother, wife and three friends — identified the accused correctly. Such flawless identification and their statements before the court helped in securing the conviction,” Mahalingappa said.
The incident had taken place at Ashoknagar in Nov 2017 when 
Harish
 was standing outside his house and noticed Gerald Arokiya Raj, James Kumar and a juvenile smoking. He shouted at them and warned of legal action if they didn’t stop smoking. The three left the place but returned with other accused, armed with machetes and other sharp objects.
They attacked Harish, who was standing with three friends. Hearing the commotion, his mother and wife came out and witnessed the murder.

stories.headline: Bengaluru Police Inspector killed in road accident in Madhya Pradesh during cybercrime investigation
stories.deck: The deceased was part of a team that went to Madhya Pradesh to pursue a lead in a cybercrime case
stories.bodyText:
A cybercrime investigator from Karnataka, who was in Madhya Pradesh as part of an investigation, lost his life in a bus accident in Rajgarh district on Friday morning, police sources said. His colleagues were also injured in the accident.
The deceased, K.B. Ravi, was deputed at the Southeast CEN Police Station in Bengaluru. Ravi and his team had travelled to Madhya Pradesh to pursue a lead in a cybercrime case.
According to police sources, the team was travelling in a local bus from Bhopal to Indore. When the bus was in Rajgarh district, the vehicle lost control and fell into a gorge near the Bhopal Bypass. Ravi was thrown out of the bus by the impact of the crash. He succumbed to his injuries, police said.
Two more officers from the same police station suffered multiple injuries but are out of danger. The Bhopal police handed over the body to the Bengaluru City Police, which brought it to Bengaluru on Friday night. M.A. Saleem, Director-General of Police, and other senior officers received the body at the HAL Airport and subsequently took it to a hall at the City Armed Reserve in Adugodi for public viewing.
Ravi was a 2007-batch officer known for his calm personality in the department. He was serving at the Ashok Nagar Police Station before being transferred to the Southeast CEN Police Station, where he handled several high-profile cases. Several inspectors posted at city police stations are batchmates of Ravi and described him as a humble, honest, and intelligent officer.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar expressed condolences to his family and said, “I too share in the grief of his family and the Police Department, who have lost such a dedicated officer. briefs.headline: Bengaluru peptide party called off as FDA inspects company
briefs.deck: A planned peptide party in Bengaluru was cancelled after regulatory action. The Food Safety and Drug Administration inspected the organizers' company and issued a notice. Officials took cognisance of social media posts advertising the event. Expired food items were also seized from medical college hostel canteens. Legal action is being initiated against the food business operators for violations.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The ‘peptide party’ planned in Bengaluru on August 29, which had drawn mixed responses online, has been cancelled after the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) inspected the organisers’ company and issued a notice.
Billed as the first event of its kind in Bengaluru, the party was to feature “peptide tastings” and was scheduled for 6.30pm Saturday in Koramangala.
According to social media posts by the hosts, the invite-only event was capped at 50 members and was to feature music, food and networking.
The posts were taken down Friday.
Peptides are short chains of amino acids that act as building blocks or signalling molecules in the body.
Peptide parties are described online as informal gatherings where people learn about, and sometimes use or sell, peptide-based products, often marketed for weight loss, anti-ageing, fitness or wellness.
FDA officials said they took cognisance of the event after seeing the social media posts and subsequently visited the office of the company hosting it.
“We did not know what kind of products they were using at the party. 
Hence, our drug inspectors visited their office and issued a notice. One of their representatives appeared before us and we asked them to provide additional details of the party,” said Srinivas K, commissioner, FDA.
A public advisory issued by the Karnataka FDA Friday identified Upsurge Labs LLP as the organisers of the event.
The advisory said the company’s authorised representatives, following an enquiry, had communicated that the scheduled event stood cancelled. It also said the representatives had requested suitable time to produce documents relating to the event.
When TOI checked with the hosts, they confirmed cancellation of the event.
Expired food seized from college hostel canteens
Food safety officials inspected 34 canteens and kitchens operating in govt and private medical college hostels across the city Thursday and issued notices to five establishments for various violations.
During the inspections, officials found labelling-related violations in one canteen and seized 7kg of expired rava and 8 litres of expired milk stored in the kitchen.
Authorities said legal action is being initiated against the food business operator concerned under the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.
The case will be placed before the adjudicating officer, the additional deputy commissioner’s court, for further proceedings.
The inspections were part of ongoing efforts to ensure food safety and hygiene standards in hostel kitchens catering to students.

briefs.headline: Dasara jumbo Srirama panics at Mysuru palace, here’s how jumbos are prepared for the festivities
briefs.bodyText:
A brief scare at Mysuru Palace on Friday highlighted why Dasara elephants need careful preparation before the grand Jamboo Savari. Dasara jumbo Srirama, who was calm moments earlier, suddenly panicked when musicians began beating drums loudly behind him. His mahout and kavadi quickly brought him under control.
The incident also underlines the importance of weeks of training and acclimatisation that the jumbos undergo before Dasara. The Forest Department, veterinarians, mahouts and kavadis work together to ensure the elephants are physically fit and accustomed to the sights and sounds of the city. As part of their preparation, the elephants are taken on regular walks along the Jamboo Savari route between Mysuru Palace and Bannimantap. They are gradually exposed to traffic, crowds, music and other sounds they may encounter during the festivities.
For Dasara 2026, a team of 12 elephants has been selected, with the first batch already arriving in Mysuru.
Getting used to the city
- Acclimatisation walks: Jumbos are taken along the Jamboo Savari route between Mysuru Palace and Bannimantap to get used to traffic, crowds, vehicles and music. 
- Load training: Elephants are gradually trained to carry procession loads. The Golden Howdah elephant undergoes special conditioning, with the weight increased gradually. 
- Sound training: Cannon-firing rehearsals and exposure to crowds and loud sounds help them adjust to the atmosphere of Dasara. 
- Special diet: Meals are planned according to age, weight and workload and include green fodder, sugarcane, rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, jaggery and coconut. 
- Health checks: Veterinarians monitor their food intake, appetite, digestion, movement and behaviour. 
- Daily care: Baths, grooming and massages are part of their routine, with mahouts and kavadis closely involved in their everyday care.
- Trust matters: Mahouts and kavadis spend weeks feeding, bathing, walking and communicating with the elephants, building familiarity and trust. 
- Safety first: By Vijayadashami, the jumbos have undergone weeks of training, nutrition, healthcare and acclimatisation to help keep both the elephants and people around them safe.

briefs.headline: Bescom’s Gruha Jyothi verification drive meets locked gates in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The gates of the city’s large apartment complexes and gated communities are proving harder for Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (Bescom) officials to cross than expected, with several residential communities denying entry to verification teams and emerging as a major hurdle in the Gruha Jyothi beneficiary verification drive.
The problem is particularly acute in the Bengaluru Metropolitan Area Zone (BMAZ), especially eastern Bengaluru, where a large number of consumers live in apartments and gated communities. With just two days left for the two-month verification deadline, Bescom has verified around 66% of its 68.9 lakh Gruha Jyothi beneficiaries, leaving a substantial number yet to be covered.
The difficulty in Bengaluru is part of a larger challenge faced by all five electricity supply companies (Escoms) as they race to complete verification under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. Collectively, Escoms have verified around 1.2 crore, or 71%, of the nearly 1.7 crore beneficiaries across 
Karnataka
. With just two days left, the utilities are awaiting govt nod to extend the exercise by another month to ensure complete verification.
Among the five Escoms, Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (Mescom) has recorded the highest progress at 90%, followed by Hubballi Electricity Supply Company (Hescom) at 79%, Bescom at 66%, Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC) at 64%, and Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company (Gescom) at 54%, according to energy department data.
A senior energy official said the verification process slowed in Aug because meter readers had to juggle the exercise with their regular responsibility of generating monthly electricity bills. 
“During July, it was easier as meter readers had to do only verification and did not have to worry about monthly bills, as average bills were generated. But in Aug, they had to do both. Further, the non-availability of working professionals during verification time also posed a challenge,” the official said.
Officials said several gated communities remain out of reach, making it difficult for verification teams to reach individual households. Door-locked homes and consumers working in other cities or abroad have also contributed to the backlog. Officials estimate that around 20% of consumers yet to be covered fall into categories such as door-locked households, apartment communities, and consumers away from home.
Bescom has introduced a mechanism to deal with locked households. Managing director N Shiva Shankara said, “Our mobile app allows staff to mark a household as ‘door-locked’ after three unsuccessful visits. An SMS is then sent to the consumer asking them to contact divisional engineers or other officials. With mutual coordination and pre-decided timings, our staffers go to their households and complete the process.”

briefs.headline: Bengaluru citizens take postcard route to oppose Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Citizens, activists and walkers have launched a postcard campaign urging govt to scrap the proposed Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road project, which is expected to pass beneath Lalbagh and require over five acres of the garden’s land.
The postcards, addressed to chief minister DK Shivakumar, call for no part of Lalbagh to be used for shafts, a multilevel parking facility or any other project-related structures. Campaigners have also urged govt to withdraw the recent amendment to Karnataka Parks (Preservation) Act, which allows up to 5% of park land to be diverted for infrastructure projects.
Environmentalist and retired IFS officer AN Yellappa Reddy, who launched the campaign, urged students from schools and colleges, children, seniors and other citizens to write individual letters to the chief minister.
BV Sridhar Rao, a regular Lalbagh walker for three decades, appealed to citizens to participate in large numbers. “People across age groups must come together to save Bengaluru’s heritage and environment by writing to the CM to drop the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel project,” he said.
Environmentalist Vijay Nishant questioned why govts had failed to recognise Lalbagh’s heritage and environmental importance. “This is a campaign aimed at saving our parks. 
I urge all citizens to support the campaign, raise awareness through WhatsApp and write a letter each,” he said.
Another citizen, in a letter to Shivakumar, urged him not to “behave like a dictator” and warned that the project could have electoral consequences. “If you want to become CM again, you must stop such projects. If you stop this, we will not vote for you in 2028,” he said.
No diversion plan yet
Regarding the possibility of diverting the tunnel road to exclude Lalbagh from its route, B-Smile technical director BS Prahallad told 
TOI
 no such plan was being considered as of now. “This is a PPC contract planned under the build, own, operate and transfer (BOOT) model. As of now, we do not have any plans to make a diversion. The decision must come from higher authorities, and we cannot speculate,” he said.
Govt had estimated the cost of the 17km tunnel road project at Rs 17,698 crore. In Dec 2025, 
Adani Group
 emerged as the lowest bidder, quoting Rs 22,267 crore for the project.

briefs.headline: National Security Guard begins month-long specialised counter-terror training for 500 cops in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: National Security Guard (NSG) has commenced a month-long specialised training programme for around 500 Karnataka police personnel, aimed at strengthening their preparedness to tackle terrorism, security breaches and other critical emergencies.
The training will cover several specialised operational areas, including counter-terrorist interventions, counter-drone operations, unarmed combat (Krav Maga), close protection, sniper training, tactical hostage negotiations, K9 operations, counter-IED operations, tactical driving and bomb disposal. The programme is designed to enhance the operational capabilities of police personnel drawn from various operational and support units across the state. As first responders during emergencies, police personnel are often the first to reach an incident site, secure the area, protect civilians and contain threats until specialised forces arrive.
The training programme was inaugurated by chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday at Manekshaw Parade Ground, where NSG demonstrated its capabilities across various operational domains at MG Road Metro station, Barton Centre and other places. briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: 
Karnataka
 will mark the birth centenary of late chief minister Ramakrishna Hegde on Aug 29, with central and state functionaries expected to attend the celebrations.

stories.headline: Inflation data 'concerning': Fed chair Warsh signals rates may need to rise
stories.deck: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has signaled that interest rates might rise in the near future, given that inflation continues to far exceed the central bank's two percent goal. He raised concerns about the persistent underlying price pressures, which have not shown significant improvement. This news prompted bond markets to adjust their forecasts, indicating a likely rate hike on the horizon.…
stories.bodyText:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has indicated that the US central bank may need to raise interest rates in the coming months if inflation does not make enough progress towards its 2% target.
Speaking at the Fed’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, Warsh acknowledged that recent US data showed inflation had cooled somewhat. However, he said the figures did not indicate a meaningful improvement in underlying price pressures.
“They do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved. We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed,” Warsh said, adding, “Otherwise, we have work to do.”
The Fed chief did not suggest a rate hike was imminent, but his comments offered a clearer indication of his concerns about inflation. They also appeared to reassure Wall Street that controlling price pressures remains a priority for the central bank.
Inflation remains well above Fed's target
Inflation stood at 3.7% in July according to the Fed’s preferred measure, well above its 2% target. Price pressures had cooled in June and July after rising sharply in May as gas prices surged.
Warsh said inflation data “are more concerning” than trends in the labour market, where unemployment remains low. He also said inflation was unlikely to return to the Fed’s target on its own.
More than half of the goods and services tracked by the government recorded price increases of 3% or more over the past year. While that was down from the pandemic peak, it remained “well above” the roughly one-third that recorded such increases in the two decades before the pandemic.
Markets raise rate-hike expectations
The speech pushed expectations for higher short-term interest rates higher in the bond market, although US stocks remained steady.
The two-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks expectations for the Fed’s federal funds rate, rose from 4.22% to 4.30%.
Investors now see the chances of a rate hike at the Fed’s September 15-16 meeting as roughly even, according to futures pricing tracked by CME FedWatch. Before Warsh spoke, the probability was about one-third.
Longer-term Treasury yields were mostly unchanged. The 10-year and 30-year yields showed little movement, suggesting investors did not expect higher rates to remain necessary for a prolonged period to tackle inflation.
Jon Faust, an economist at Johns Hopkins and former adviser to Jerome Powell, said Warsh had conveyed a tougher approach to inflation without giving the detailed policy guidance he has criticised.
“He found a way to convey that if necessary he would support raising rates, which is one thing people were concerned about,” Faust said.
Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, said Warsh had previously spoken toughly about inflation without raising the Fed’s key rate. He said Friday’s comments did not provide clearer guidance on the timing of a possible move.
Warsh avoids 'forward guidance'
Warsh’s speech came after his July 29 press conference created uncertainty over whether his tough comments on inflation would be followed by action.
The Fed’s short-term interest rate is currently about 3.6%. Warsh has said he does not want to provide “forward guidance” on whether the central bank will raise, cut or hold rates at upcoming meetings.
He argues that committing to a particular policy path would limit the Fed’s flexibility. Some economists have said he could offer more insight into his views without signalling a specific future action.
Warsh reiterated his scepticism towards such guidance on Friday.
He also suggested that current interest rates were not restricting economic activity, pointing to strong consumer spending and robust business investment in AI equipment and infrastructure.
Fed chair clarifies policy approach
Warsh also sought to clear up confusion from his July 29 news conference over the inflation measure used by the Fed and its main tool for fighting price pressures.
On Friday, he specified that short-term interest rates are the Fed’s “predominant tool” and said the central bank is using the same gauge it has long followed to measure inflation.
Fed chairs have often used Jackson Hole speeches to discuss broad economic and monetary policy questions or signal changes in their approach. In 2022, Powell used the event to signal that the Fed would continue sharply raising rates after pandemic-era inflation reached 9.1%, warning that the measures would bring “pain” to consumers and businesses.
Trump keeps pressure on Fed
Warsh’s approach is being closely observed as US President Donald Trump continues to call for lower interest rates. Trump has defended Warsh, whom he appointed, while criticising other Fed officials who support higher rates.
Trump has also renewed efforts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook, appointed by former President Joe Biden. Replacing Cook would allow Trump to appoint a majority of the seven-member board. The US President tried to fire her last year but was temporarily blocked by the Supreme Court.
Longer-term rates have risen in recent weeks amid factors including growing US government deficits and heavy borrowing by technology firms building AI infrastructure.
The 30-year Treasury yield reached a 19-year high last week, prompting US treasury secretary Scott Bessent to make an unusual effort to buy back bonds and push yields lower.
Warsh replaced Powell as Fed chair in late May after his predecessor’s term ended.

stories.headline: IGL hikes CNG prices by ₹3.89 per kg as LNG prices stay elevated
stories.deck: This would be the fifth such increase since the onset of the conflict in West Asia
stories.bodyText:
North India’s largest city-gas distributor Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) informed late on Friday (August 28, 2026) that it would be increasing the price of compressed natural gas (CNG) across all its retail stations by ₹3.89 per kg as international prices of the input gas, that is, LNG, continues to remain elevated amid the re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia, effective Saturday (August 29, 2026).
With the latest revision, the vehicular gas in Delhi would now cost ₹86.98 per kilogram. Friday’s (August 28, 2026) hike would be the fifth such increase since the onset of the conflict in West Asia.
In a statement, IGL explained that re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia has continued to affect cargo movement across the Strait of Hormuz. As a result, it observed, “Global LNG prices have nearly doubled as compared to pre-crisis period. Additionally, there is an urgency in Europe to increase their natural gas storage on account of approaching winter season.”
It added that a significant portion of requirements are being met through the more expensive spot purchases.
Thus, it stated, “With international LNG prices remaining elevated and the cost impact becoming increasingly significant, a calibrated revision of ₹3.89 per kg has now become necessary to partially offset the increase in input gas cost while ensuring continuity and reliability of CNG supplies.”
Before this, the price of CNG in several cities of North India had increased cumulatively by ₹6 per kg across four tranches since May 15.

stories.headline: CNG price hike: Compressed natural gas gets costlier; check city-wise rates

Effective August 29, this change is linked to surging international LNG prices and ongoing Middle East conflicts, impacting both freight and passenger fares in the region, following several prior…
stories.bodyText:
Compressed natural gas
 (CNG) consumers in Delhi and several other cities will have to pay more from Saturday, with Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) announcing a Rs 3.89 per kg increase in prices amid a sharp rise in the cost of imported liquefied natural gas (LNG). The revised rates will come into effect from August 29.
CNG will now cost Rs 86.98 per kg in Delhi while in Noida and Ghaziabad, the revised price will be Rs 95.59 per kg. Gurugram consumers will pay Rs 92.01 per kg.
IGL said the price revision was driven by higher international LNG prices, as a large portion of the gas used for CNG comes from imports. Spot LNG prices have risen sharply since the Middle East conflict began.
"With international LNG prices remaining elevated and the cost impact becoming increasingly significant, a calibrated revision of Rs 3.89 per kg has now become necessary to partially offset the increase in input gas cost," IGL said.
How much CNG costs in your city
CNG prices differ across states because of variations in value-added tax structures, similar to petrol and diesel.
The latest hike is the fifth increase in CNG prices this year and comes after the previous revision in May, when IGL raised prices by a cumulative Rs 6 per kg in four phases over 10 days. That increase followed a global rise in energy prices amid the Middle East conflict.
Higher CNG prices have also affected freight and passenger fares in Delhi-NCR, where most auto-rickshaws, taxis and goods carriers run on the fuel.
The conflict has continued for almost six months, while crude prices have risen above $90 per barrel. However, prices remain well below the earlier peak of $126 per barrel recorded during the previous phase of the conflict.

stories.headline: Fiscal federalism, efficiency versus equity concerns
stories.deck: The Sixteenth Finance Commission risks moving away from its core mandate of acting as an equalising force within the federation
stories.bodyText:
The Finance Commission, an institutional innovation embedded in India’s constitutional architecture, was never intended to be a routine allocator of funds. It was designed as a central pillar of India’s fiscal federal compact and as a corrective institution that would mediate the inherent asymmetry between a fiscally dominant Union and structurally constrained States, while also addressing deep horizontal inequalities arising from history, geography, and institutional capacity. In a country marked by uneven development at Independence, the Commission’s central mandate was to safeguard the interests of the States and thereby preserve a strong Union.
Each successive Commission, cognisant of its historical context, has interpreted this mandate in its own way, yet all have contributed to sustaining India’s fiscal federal compact. The recently submitted report of the 16th Finance Commission (FC-16), chaired by Arvind Panagariya and covering the period 2026-31, marks a decisive turning point. While it retains the vertical devolution of central taxes to the States at 41%, it fundamentally re-engineers the structure of fiscal transfers, particularly grants-in-aid. In doing so, it prioritises efficiency and performance but raises serious concerns about equity and constitutional intent. At the heart of the issue lies a deeper question: has the Commission moved away from its equalising role toward one that implicitly protects the Union’s fiscal primacy?
The constitutional logic of grants-in-aid
Evidently, the provision for grants-in-aid under Article 275 was not an afterthought; it was a foundational design element. In a country more diverse than any other in the world, tax devolution, however sophisticated its formula, cannot account for the diversity of State-specific needs. For instance, Kerala’s “export-oriented” human capital development strategy has accounted for nearly 23% of India’s total remittances, thereby strengthening the country’s external sector. However, this has come at a cost to the State’s fiscal health, as it has had to rely on borrowing to finance investments in education.
Editorial | A cautious nudge: On the 16th Finance Commission’s recommendations
Similarly, Punjab has played a critical role in ensuring national food security, but at the cost of its revenue base, by focusing on the production of wheat and rice, which are non-taxable apart from paying the price of being a border State. The same is true of the hill States, which face high infrastructure costs; the north-eastern States, which grapple with connectivity constraints; and fiscally stressed States burdened by demographic pressures and social sector commitments.
Grants-in-aid were therefore conceived as instruments of equalisation, enabling targeted support for States with special needs where formula-based tax devolution falls short. The F-14 and the FC-15 recognised this reality by retaining Revenue Deficit Grants (RDGs), sector-specific grants, and State-specific grants.
The FC-16 departs sharply from this tradition. It recommends grants-in-aid of ₹9.47 lakh crore, compared with ₹10.1 lakh crore under the FC-15, while their share in total Finance Commission transfers has more than halved, from 19.4% to 8.3%. By restricting grants-in-aid to local bodies and disaster management, it eliminates RDGs, sector-specific grants, and State-specific grants.
While retaining the States’ share in the divisible pool at 41%, despite the demand from 18 States to raise it to 50%, the Commission presumes that improved fiscal discipline should enable States to manage their finances without additional gap-filling transfers. However, this reasoning rests on a problematic assumption: that fiscal capacity across States is sufficiently uniform for devolution to be self-equalising.
Empirically and historically, this assumption is untenable. The Commission’s justification for doing away with RDGs is rooted in concerns about fiscal prudence. It argues that RDGs create moral hazard by incentivising States to underperform in revenue mobilisation or overspend in the expectation of central support.
It also points to aggregate data suggesting that the States, taken as a whole, are not in severe fiscal distress. Yet, this aggregate view masks deep inter-State disparities, with some States remaining fiscally stressed despite contributing disproportionately to national development and continuing to require fiscal assistance. The very purpose of RDGs was to recognise this heterogeneity, as a fiscal surplus in one State cannot offset a fiscal deficit in another.
More troubling is the contrast between the Commission’s stance on RDGs and its treatment of cesses and surcharges. While advocating fiscal discipline for States through the withdrawal of RDGs, it stops short of recommending any binding rollback of these non-shareable union levies ignoring the demand by many States.
Dual shift
Instead, it proposes a “grand bargain”, whereby the Centre would gradually merge cesses into the divisible pool in exchange for States accepting a lower devolution share. This asymmetry is difficult to overlook. RDGs are removed in the name of discipline, yet cesses — arguably a more distortionary instrument from a federal perspective — are only gently nudged toward reform. The resulting framework imposes stringency on States while preserving fiscal flexibility for the Union. This dual shift, protecting Union revenues while constraining State support, raises a fundamental concern: is the Commission inadvertently reinforcing vertical imbalance rather than correcting it?
The consequences are particularly severe for States that already face structural disadvantages. As many as eight States, including most of the disadvantaged north-eastern States and fiscally stressed West Bengal, are set to experience a reduced share in both tax devolution and grants-in-aid, while another six States have seen a decline in their share of grants. The problem is further compounded by the reduction in the weight assigned to income distance (from 45% to 42.5%) and the introduction of a 10% weight for contribution to GDP. When combined with the removal of the RDGs, which accounted for about 20% of Finance Commission grants in 2024-25, this creates a double burden: lower tax devolution and the absence of compensatory grants. The Commission’s implicit assumption that efficiency should trump equity risks widening regional disparities.
Another defining feature of the FC-16 is its emphasis on tied and performance-based grants, particularly for local governments. While the allocation of nearly ₹7.2 lakh crore to the third tier is commendable, the conditionalities attached to these grants are stringent, linking the release of funds to targets in water and sanitation, revenue mobilisation, and audited accounts. This approach promotes accountability, but it also reduces fiscal autonomy. In effect, the architecture of grants shifts from need-based equalisation to compliance-based incentivisation. Fiscal discipline, while necessary, cannot substitute for fiscal justice.
Efficiency versus equity
The FC-16’s report is bold in ambition but uneven in balance. The dismantling of the RDGs and the shift toward performance-based transfers reflect a technocratic confidence in market-like incentives, even though fiscal federalism is a political and constitutional arrangement designed to manage diversity. The contrast between the Commission’s strict stance on RDGs and its accommodative approach to cesses and surcharges, along with its hesitation to raise the States’ share in the divisible pool to 50% despite demands from several States, reveals a deeper tension.
It suggests a framework that, intentionally or otherwise, protects the fiscal space of the Union while placing a greater adjustment burden on the States. In doing so, the Commission may have moved away from its core mandate of acting as an equalising force within the federation. If the Finance Commission is to continue playing its historic role in holding India together, future Commissions must reward high-performing States while supporting those that continue to face structural disadvantages.
For a country as diverse as India, fiscal federalism cannot be sustained on performance alone; it must be anchored in fairness.
K.J. Joseph is Director, Gulati Institute of Finance and Taxation, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala; Sumalatha B.S. is Assistant Professor, Gulati Institute of Finance and Taxation, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. The views expressed are personal

briefs.headline: Inflation isn’t meaningfully slowing: Federal Reserve chairman
briefs.bodyText:
Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh warned inflation isn’t meaningfully slowing and said policymakers must be confident that it is, otherwise the central bank has “work to do.” In a sweeping speech, his first since becoming chairman of the central bank in May, Warsh reiterated that policymakers will return inflation to their 2% goal, which he said is a firm and fixed target.
“Here is my standard: We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do. That’s our job,” Warsh said in remarks prepared for Fed’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.
Warsh said financial conditions are not restrictive and interest rates are Fed’s “predominant tool” for achieving its mandate, though he stopped short of signaling he would support an interest-rate hike when Fed officials gather in Sept. “I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision.” Yields for two-year Treasuries rose five basis points to 4.28%, while 30-year rates slipped — signal of an expectation that Fed may need to raise short-term rates.

briefs.headline: Noel Tata, Shapoorji discuss share swap for Tata Sons stake sale
briefs.bodyText:
The 
Tata Group
 is in talks with its biggest minority shareholder on proposals to unlock liquidity, including a potential swap of shares of its listed entities, as the Shapoorji Pallonji Group seeks funds to repay costly debt, according to sources.
Representatives of Noel Tata, the Tata family patriarch, are exploring the possibility where SP Group receives shares of companies such as Tata Power Co in exchange for some or all of its 18.4% in the privately-held Tata Sons Pvt, the sources said, asking not to be identified as the discussions are private.
Two other options have also been presented: a direct buyout of the construction giant’s stake by Tata Sons, financed by overseas banks, or a sale to an external investor, preferably a global one, the sources added.
Any breakthrough on this long-running tussle between the Tatas and the SP Group will prove to be a windfall for investors in the latter’s debt, which include the likes of Cerberus Capital Management LP, Davidson Kempner Capital Management and Farallon Capital Management. For the Tatas, a resolution may ease some of the intense regulatory spotlight it has come under in the past few years after RBI rules revived pressure on its holding company to list on the exchanges.
Noel is the chairman of Tata Trusts, a group of charities that own 66% in Tata Sons. Natarajan Chandrasekaran’s announcement this month that he’ll step down as Tata Sons chairman in Feb has put Noel in the driver’s seat to drive a settlement. Noel also has familial connections: he is married to Aloo Mistry, the sister of SP Group chairman Shapoor Mistry.
Representatives of Tata Sons and Shapoorji Pallonji Group did not offer any immediate comments.
SP Group closed one of the largest private credit transactions in India in July, as investors are hopeful that the conglomerate can eventually monetise its stake in Tata Sons and unlock liquidity worth billions of rupees.
There’s no certainty that the ongoing talks will lead to a deal and the structure of the transaction may change as negotiations proceed, the sources said. A major hurdle will be in agreeing at a valuation for Tata Sons that controls bulk of the sprawling salt-to-software conglomerate and has many large unlisted businesses such as Air India Ltd and iPhone maker Tata Electronics Pvt Ltd under its umbrella. Both sides are evaluating legal aspects of all options being discussed as well as potential regulatory issues around the share swap since it will involve listed Tata entities, the sources said. SP Group is also periodically updating its stakeholders on the negotiations, while advisers are examining the legal implications of the various structures under consideration, they said.
A resolution needs to come through within the next 18 months as that is the timeline when SP Group’s recently closed bond issue will need to make its first payout. These bonds sold by Eqyizen Investment offered 18.95% and will mature in 36 months. The first interest payment is coming up in July 2028.

briefs.headline: RBI push: Forex reserves at all-time high of $729.3bn
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The country’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $12.4 billion in the week ended Aug 21, to an all-time high of $729.3 billion, driven largely by non-resident deposits drawn through a special scheme under which RBI took over the foreign currency risks from banks. Foreign currency assets, the largest component, rose $9.5 billion to $591.3 billion, while gold reserves increased $2.8 billion to $114.2 billion.
The previous record was $728.5 billion on Feb 27, 2026, just before the outbreak of the US-Iran war. Higher crude oil prices and pressure on the rupee subsequently prompted RBI intervention, taking reserves to a low of $666.9 billion on June 26.
The largest weekly increase in total reserves was recorded in the week ended Aug 27, 2021, when reserves rose sharply following a major allocation of special drawing rights by the IMF.
For the financial year so far, total reserves have increased by $38.2 billion from end-March 2026. FCA have risen $39.1 billion, more than the overall increase, while gold reserves have declined $1.2 billion.
The recent rise in reserves, particularly FCA, has been supported by RBI measures to attract dollar inflows and manage rupee volatility. In June, RBI and govt launched a concessional USD-INR forex swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings and ECBs.
The facility has mobilised an estimated $65 billion to $73 billion ahead of its Aug 31 closure.
